rows.title: Legacy preset additional-parameter save, apply, and reset
observables: The selected preset snapshots the outgoing global additionalParams value before switching.
The incoming preset applies its additionalParams value without aliasing the stored preset array.
Missing, null, empty, legacy, and non-default values remain distinguishable until the owning normalization rule applies.
The selected value survives SQLite persistence and bootstrap reload.
variants: saveCurrent false and apply false pointer-only selection
normalization: JSON object-key order is ignored.
Array order, missing, null, empty array, and default are semantic and must not be normalized together.

tests: server/fastify/__tests__/commands.test.ts (legacy preset additionalParams save/apply/reset, persistence, and bootstrap matrix)

verification.residual: The baseline omitted this field, so this is verified as an additive Fastify-only preservation rule rather than fork-point parity.

rows.notes: This pilot traces a recent field-completeness omission rather than claiming that the baseline itself preserved preset-scoped additional parameters.

rows.title: Translation preset and model-profile runtime dispatch
observables: Translation uses the selected global or chat-bound translator preset.
An LLM step resolves the selected model profile, model ID, endpoint, runtime options, and additional parameters.
Missing or invalid profile bindings follow the documented legacy/default path rather than a stale profile.
Provider failure returns the translation failure contract without caching a false success.
Preset and profile selection survive reload.
variants: profile with non-default sampler and endpoint options
normalization: Credential bytes are redacted while credential selection and presence remain semantic.
Endpoint path/query, model ID, option values, step order, missing, null, and default are semantic.

verification.residual: The profile abstraction is post-baseline; live third-party transport remains deterministically stubbed while selection, request shape, failure, and reload are production-path tested.

rows.notes: The comparison preserves the baseline's selected translation intent while allowing the Fastify profile representation to differ physically.

rows.title: OpenAI Responses endpoint and request-shape preservation
observables: An explicit model endpoint overrides the generic custom URL.
An already complete Responses path and query string are preserved exactly.
Autofill appends /responses or /v1/responses without moving query parameters.
Request body, resolved model/options, streaming mode, and retry/fallback selection remain owned by the same resolved profile.
normalization: Authorization values are redacted while header presence and credential selection remain semantic.
URL path/query, array order, body values, missing, null, and defaults are semantic; JSON object-key order alone is ignored.

verification.residual: Live third-party retry behavior is fixture-proven rather than exercised against a paid endpoint.

rows.notes: The explicit endpoint rule is byte-for-byte semantic; normalizers may not erase path or query differences.

rows.title: Portable reroll-candidate ordering and identity
observables: Every retained candidate is exported in newest-to-oldest navigation order.
Candidate role, text, message identity, generation metadata, and references survive supported round trips.
Portable import extracts candidates into durable alternate rows without duplicating them into the active transcript.
Hydration and reload reconstruct the candidate buffer so forward/back navigation restores the same displaced tail.
variants: candidate with generationInfo and reference metadata
Original-style block and local-backup codec round trip
normalization: Generated IDs may be normalized only when occurrence order and every identity/reference relationship remain intact.
Candidate order, role, repeated values, metadata presence, missing, null, and empty arrays are semantic.

tests: server/fastify/__tests__/risuSaveCodec.test.ts (export, decode, fresh import, and reload through all supported codecs)

verification.residual: All current raw, compressed, stream, and block .risu codecs pass an exported-byte round trip. Direct execution inside Original RisuAI is infeasible because the pinned harness exposes no save-exchange or durable-reroll seam; reopen when such a seam exists.

rows.notes: Original retained candidates only in a process-local buffer; the Fastify-only persistence must remain additive and must not make shared saves unreadable.

rows.title: Closed trigger modes, effects, ordering, mutable state, and unsupported boundaries
observables: All six trigger modes, four condition kinds, 118 effect kinds, and four regex stages are classified as implemented or explicitly unsupported.
Input, start, request, output, and display execution preserve effect order, prior durable variable writes, recursion budgets, and transient-output rollback on a retained whole-trigger guard.
Forty unsupported effect kinds cannot silently perform partial persistent mutation.
variants: input, start, manual, request, output, and display
condition miss, stop, recursion, malformed container variable, and state effect in the wrong mode
durable script variables, transient chat/prompt output, and unsupported effects
normalization: Generated diagnostics may sanitize paths; effect order, variable values, transcript identity/content, provider-call count, unsupported kind, and abort boundary remain semantic.

rows.title: Closed Lua API, regex transformation, execution-bound, and automation failure ownership
observables: Browser and Fastify declare the same 54 Lua host APIs, each classified as supported, browser-UI no-op, interactive rejection, or media-read rejection.
Global and local regex stages preserve order, fresh global/sticky state, unmatched group behavior, compatibility bounds, and visible failure.
Timeout, recursion, parser, regex, and host-API failures stop before destructive or paid side effects according to their owning stage.
variants: 54 Lua APIs and every script mode
global, module, character, and preset regex stages
success, compile failure, runtime failure, timeout, recursion exhaustion, cancellation, and unsupported host API
normalization: Stack paths and wall-clock durations may be sanitized; API name, mode, input/output text, transform order, regex captures, durable writes, failure class, and provider-call absence remain semantic.
rows.notes: Signed Lua state and failure differences remain independently governed; this row owns the closed supported API and transformation surface.

rows.title: Closed Plugin V3 API, permission, RPC, runtime, and sandbox boundary
observables: Every one of the 85 direct V3 API keys has exactly one capability classification and the browser/server gate accepts only API version 3.0.
All nine permissions, four runtime phases, and seven RPC message types have a production owner.
Plugin network, storage, host-DOM, callback, abort, and iframe CSP boundaries cannot silently bypass their permission or lifecycle owner.
variants: install, load, ready, error, unload, and reload
granted, denied, missing, and revoked permissions
direct API, instance API, callbacks, abort signals, storage, network, and DOM access
normalization: Generated plugin instance/callback ids may be normalized; API key, permission, phase, RPC type, call order, result/error, abort, storage mutation, and network target remain semantic.

verification.residual: The V3 runtime is a trusted DOM-compatible extension boundary, not a hostile-code security sandbox; deterministic tests own API/CSP/permission behavior, while no real-browser V3 iframe journey is currently tracked.

rows.notes: The closed API catalog fails when any key, permission, runtime phase, or RPC type is added without classification.

rows.title: Module artifact, activation, command, persistence, and import/export lifecycle
observables: All seven module activation sources resolve enablement and order through one shared lifecycle.
Create, import, edit, enable, disable, reorder, character selection, delete, reload, and .risum export preserve identity, metadata, references, and persistence.
Module import rejects non-importable MCP identifiers before durable mutation.
variants: global, chat, character, persona, prompt-preset, agent-preset, and legacy integration
json, lorebook, and risum import plus risum export
create, patch, enable, reorder, select, delete, reload, and MCP validation
normalization: Generated module ids and timestamps may be normalized; name, metadata, content, enabled state, source, order, references, selected character, MCP identifiers, bytes, and reload result remain semantic.

verification.residual: Deterministic browser/server suites own module lifecycle and bytes; a production-bundle module-picker/import journey is not separately tracked.

rows.notes: Character/module conversion is excluded here and remains independently governed by ORC-SURFACE-062.

rows.title: MCP identifier, registry, transport, OAuth, egress, aggregation, and cancellation ownership
observables: Internal, plugin, stdio-wrapper, and remote HTTP identifier classes have explicit import and runtime dispositions.
Six internal clients, remote discovery, duplicate-tool aggregation, call-only restrictions, cancellation, OAuth refresh, and DNS-pinned egress have one owner each.
Unsupported command-based stdio use and invalid identifiers fail visibly before registration or tool execution.
variants: internal, plugin, stdio wrapper, localhost HTTP, and remote HTTPS identifiers
discovery, initialize, list tools, duplicate names, call, cancel, close, and reconnect
OAuth refresh success/failure and public/private/mixed DNS resolution
normalization: Session ids, request ids, timestamps, and OAuth expiry wall time may be normalized; identifier, server capabilities, tool names/order, arguments, results/errors, call cardinality, cancellation, token replacement, and resolved address class remain semantic.

verification.residual: No deterministic CI case uses a real remote standards-conformant MCP server across discovery, OAuth, streaming/SSE, result, cancellation, and reconnect; protocol and egress seams are covered independently.

rows.title: Specialized and Risu-access tool catalogs, validation, authority, and durable failure behavior
observables: File System, AI access, Google Search, GraphMem, Dice, and Risu-access advertise exact non-duplicated tool catalogs.
Tool arguments, permissions, file authority, browser/server availability, cancellation, and mutation staging fail before partial durable changes.
Dice work is bounded, corrupt GraphMem state is never overwritten, and a missing file-system directory points only to an advertised recovery path.

file, character, chat, module, graph-memory, dice, search, and model authority
normalization: Random dice values and generated ids may be controlled/normalized; tool name, schema, arguments, authority, result/error, limits, cancellation, durable state, and mutation cardinality remain semantic.
